text:
Ethan Park: hey folks, first week here — trying to get kubectl set up. I followed the onboarding PDF and downloaded the company kubeconfig, but when I merge it with my personal file my kubectl commands hang then timeout. Anyone know what I should check?

Ethan Park: I did: `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/downloads/company-kube.yaml kubectl get nodes` and it just stalls then: `The connection to the server 10.9.3.5:6443 was refused - did you specify the right host or port?`

DevEx Bot: welcome Ethan! :wave: quick sanity list:
• confirm the active context with `kubectl config current-context`
• run `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}'` to see which endpoint kubectl is trying to reach
• if you get an IP (10.x.x.x) that likely requires VPN or a bastion jump
• try `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/downloads/company-kube.yaml get nodes` to rule out merge problems

Ethan Park: when I `--kubeconfig` directly it returns quickly with the same timeout error, so merge probably not the issue. Server shows `https://10.9.3.5:6443`. I'm on home wifi not on VPN.

Lina M.: hey Ethan — you'll need VPN for 10.x internal IPs. We also provide a remote-access LB for long-term remote devs; ping platform if you need one. For now, use the bastion: `ssh -J eth-bastion.company.internal -L 6443:10.9.3.5:6443 me@jump` then in another terminal `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/downloads/company-kube.yaml get pods --all-namespaces`.

Ethan Park: got it. I tried the bastion tunnel and the server responded, but now I get `error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)` — my account is `ethan.park@company` and my kubeconfig user entry is `auth-provider: oidc`. The company login page said it'd auto-refresh tokens but I haven't logged in yet.

DevEx Bot: OIDC tokens often expire if you download the kubeconfig from the portal (they include a short-lived id-token). Run `company-auth login` or open the browser auth flow (`https://auth.company.internal/authorize`) to refresh. Also check `kubectl config view users` and remove stale token-type users if there are duplicates.

Ethan Park: I refreshed via `company-auth login` and retried — still Unauthorized. Here's a sanitized snippet of my current context:```
contexts:
- name: onboard-ethan@dev
  context:
    cluster: dev-cluster
    user: ethan.park@company
users:
- name: ethan.park@company
  user:
    auth-provider:
      name: oidc
      config:
        id-token: REDACTED
        refresh-token: REDACTED
```

Lina M.: that looks okay. Next check: are you in the right RBAC group? `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=onboard-ethan` will tell you. If it says no, platform needs to bind either your user or the group you're in (`eng-onboarding`) to the namespace Role.

Ethan Park: `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=onboard-ethan` returns `no`. How do I request the role?

Platform Oncall: @Ethan I can do a temporary grant. Please paste `kubectl config view --minify --raw | grep -E "user:|name:" -A1` (redact tokens) and confirm the exact namespace (looks like `onboard-ethan`). I'll add a RoleBinding for `group:eng-onboarding` or `user:ethan.park@company` depending on your group membership.

Ethan Park: pasted:```
contexts:
- name: onboard-ethan@dev
  context:
    cluster: dev-cluster
    namespace: onboard-ethan
    user: ethan.park@company
users:
- name: ethan.park@company (auth-provider: oidc)
```

Platform Oncall: Thanks — looks like your identity isn't in `eng-onboarding`. I'll create a 24h RoleBinding for `user:ethan.park@company` -> `Role:onboard-namespace-reader` in `onboard-ethan` now. Let me know when you test.

Ethan Park: tried again and `kubectl get pods -n onboard-ethan` works! :relieved: Quick follow-up: is it OK to keep company kubeconfig merged into `~/.kube/config` or should I keep them separate?

Lina M.: Good question. Best practice: keep personal and company kubeconfigs separate and use `KUBECONFIG` or `--kubeconfig` while onboarding. When you want them merged, flatten and inspect before replacing `~/.kube/config`. We also recommend renaming contexts with `kubectl config rename-context` so you don't get confused between similarly-named contexts.

Ethan Park: awesome — thanks everyone for the quick help. Happy to contribute a tiny note to the onboarding doc about using the bastion tunnel for remote devs.

DevEx Bot: great idea — please open a short PR on the DevEx docs repo and tag @lina. Also: welcome to Redwood Inference, Ethan! :tada:
